findings.F1: Across all bars of folds B and C, the stretch carries both ways over 5 days, measured as the close's distance from its 20-day average in units of the 20-day standard deviation of daily returns. Closes at least 2 units below the average are followed by a 5-day excess return of -1.97 % (t -2.43, 276 cases), and closes more than 2 units above by +2.12 % (t 2.77, 284 cases). Signed in the stretch's direction, the largest-stretch cases carry +3.47 % (t 2.39 with the cases of one day taken together, 341 cases on 111 days).
findings.F2: The rank correlation between the stretch and the next 5 days' excess return is positive on all 6 coins (0.08 to 0.13). The |stretch|-weighted signed continuation is positive in 11 of the 12 windows; the only exception is w12, at -0.35 %.
findings.F3: In a choppy market (60-day return between -10 % and +10 %, calm or agitated), the |stretch|-weighted signed 5-day continuation is +5.82 % (t 2.04 by day, 125 cases on 65 days), against +1.33 % in falling markets (t 0.78).
findings.F4: Inside choppy markets the carry is larger below the average than above it. Below, the mean is -5.01 % (t -3.48, 60 cases) and reaches -11.72 % for stretches beyond 2 units (t -1.74 by day, 16 cases). Above, it is +1.78 % (t 1.25, 65 cases) and reaches +4.51 % beyond 2 units (t 1.23, 22 cases).
findings.F5: The tested book traded the choppy-agitated profile only, which holds 4.8 % of the bars. That left too few cases for its result to be told from chance (24 choppy-agitated cases at +10.19 %, t 1.02). In the calm half of choppy markets, the carry held with 101 cases at +4.63 % (t 2.06).
findings.F6: The carry also runs over 10 days: closes more than 2 units above the average are followed by +4.38 % (t 2.81, 149 cases), and those at least 2 units below by -2.59 % (t -1.97, 135 cases).
findings.F7: In rising markets the stretch also carries: +2.69 % above the average (t 2.99, 227 cases) and -2.78 % below it (t -2.00, 91 cases). This is already held by the map's rising-market range-top, nearness-to-high and breakout continuation strategies.
findings.F8: After a down day of 1 to 2 usual moves, the next day rebounds by +0.77 % over the coin's mean (t 2.12 by day, 693 cases). This is already held by the map's many agitated-fall rebound strategies, so it is not a discovery.

ideas.idea: In a choppy market, the further a coin's close stands from its 20-day average, counted in units of its 20-day standard deviation of daily returns, the more the coin keeps moving the same way over the next 5 days: further above, more rise; further below, more fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader in a coin that has gone nowhere over two months should lean with a close stretched from its 20-day average, on either side and sized by the stretch, for about a week, rather than fade it.
ideas.name: choppy stretch carries both ways

ideas.idea: In any market, the further a coin's close stands from its 20-day average, counted in units of its 20-day standard deviation of daily returns, the more the coin keeps moving the same way over the next 10 days, upward above the average and downward below it.
ideas.consequence: A trader can hold a position sized by the stretch for about two weeks, short below the average as well as long above it, a short side the map's strategies acting in every profile barely cover.
ideas.name: stretch from average carries
